Let \(\zeta=e^{2\pi i/12}\). Any 12th root of unity can be written as \(\zeta^m\). So let  
\[
a=\zeta^m,\qquad b=\zeta^n.
\]
Then
\[
(a+b)^{12}=\left(\zeta^n(\zeta^{m-n}+1)\right)^{12}
=(\zeta^n)^{12}(1+\zeta^{m-n})^{12}
=(1+\zeta^r)^{12},
\]
where \(r\equiv m-n\pmod{12}\). Thus we only need the distinct values of \((1+\zeta^r)^{12}\) for \(r=0,1,\dots,11\).

Now \(\zeta^r=e^{\pi i r/6}\), so
\[
1+\zeta^r=1+e^{\pi i r/6}
=2\cos\left(\frac{\pi r}{12}\right)e^{\pi i r/12}.
\]
Therefore
\[
(1+\zeta^r)^{12}
=2^{12}\cos^{12}\left(\frac{\pi r}{12}\right)e^{\pi i r}
=4096(-1)^r\cos^{12}\left(\frac{\pi r}{12}\right).
\]

Evaluating for \(r=0,\dots,11\), the distinct values are:
\[
4096,\quad -(2+\sqrt3)^6,\quad 729,\quad -64,\quad 1,\quad -(2-\sqrt3)^6,\quad 0.
\]
There are \(7\) distinct values.

The answer is \(\boxed{7}\).
